# emeansR

An R implementation of e-means (Bessa et al., 2026,
[arXiv:2611.09501](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09501)), a mini-batch
replacement for Lloyd’s k-means. Each centroid follows an exponential
moving average of its mini-batch means, and fitted scaling laws set the
batch size and step size, so you only supply the data, `k` and an epoch
budget. The paper reports a lower within-cluster sum of squares than 25
Lloyd iterations after a few epochs; the benchmark below shows where
that holds.

The compute core (nearest-centroid assignment and the EMA updates) is
Rust, multi-threaded on the CPU. The training recipe follows the
reference library,
[`faiss/contrib/e_means`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss/tree/main/contrib/e_means),
and gives the same batch size and step size for the same `n`, `k`, `d`
and epoch budget.

## Installation

You need a Rust toolchain (`rustc` \>= 1.71 and `cargo`):
`apt-get install cargo rustc`, `dnf install cargo`, `brew install rust`,
or [rustup](https://rustup.rs/). All Rust dependencies ship with the
package, so the build needs no network access.

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ToledoEM/emeansR")
```

## Example

``` r

library(emeansR)

set.seed(1)
centers <- matrix(rnorm(256 * 32, sd = 3), 256)
x <- centers[sample(256, 1e5, TRUE), ] + matrix(rnorm(1e5 * 32), 1e5)

fit <- emeans(x, k = 256, nepochs = 3)
fit$tot.withinss / nrow(x)    # mean squared distance to the nearest center
predict(fit, x[1:5, ])        # cluster labels for new rows
```

[`emeans()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans.md)
returns an object that also inherits from `kmeans`, with the usual
`cluster`, `centers`, `size`, `withinss` and `tot.withinss` components.

On an Apple M2 (7 threads), this example took 0.20 s with a loss of
54.7. `stats::kmeans(algorithm = "Lloyd", iter.max = 25)` from random
rows took 9.3 s and reached 64.5.

Other features:

- `spherical = TRUE` clusters unit vectors by cosine similarity.
- `precision = "single"` computes distances in float32.
- `max_points_per_centroid` trains on a random subset, as `faiss.Kmeans`
  does.
- [`emeans_stream()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans_stream.md)
  and its companions train on data supplied in chunks, for data that
  does not fit in memory.
- [`emeans_recipe()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans_recipe.md)
  shows the batch size and step size the scaling laws pick.

## Benchmark

Median time to a `k`-cluster partition for
[`emeans()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans.md),
[`kmeans()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/kmeans.html),
[`hclust()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/hclust.html) and `Mclust()` on two
synthetic scenarios (5 seeds each, Apple M2).
[`hclust()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/hclust.html) and `Mclust()` stop at
n = 10,000 because their memory grows with n².

![Median seconds to a k-cluster partition by method and data size, log
scales](reference/figures/README-benchmark-time.png)

Median seconds to a k-cluster partition by method and data size, log
scales

With 256 clusters,
[`emeans()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans.md) is
12 to 26 times faster than
[`kmeans()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/kmeans.html) (26 times at n =
500,000) at similar quality. With 20 well-separated clusters it is the
fastest method, but [`hclust()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/hclust.html)
and `Mclust()` find better partitions. The [benchmark
article](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/articles/benchmark.html) has
the quality results and caveats.

## Single-cell data

On 73,042 mouse cells from GEO
[GSE233163](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE233163)
(20 principal components, Apple M2, 7 cores for both methods), Seurat’s
neighbour graph plus Louvain at 14 resolutions took 84.5 s.
[`emeans()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans.md) at
the same 14 cluster counts took 1.1 s, and a five-level bisecting tree
(31 clusters) took 0.2 s.

![Seconds per partition and for the whole sweep, Seurat Louvain against
emeans, on 73,042 cells](reference/figures/README-single-cell-time.png)

Seconds per partition and for the whole sweep, Seurat Louvain against
emeans, on 73,042 cells

The [single-cell
article](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/articles/single-cell.html)
builds the tree, checks its stability across seeds and compares it with
Louvain and the authors’ cell types.

[`emeans()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans.md)
works on any cell embedding, so it fits a Seurat workflow after
`RunPCA()`:

### Seurat Integration with e-means

``` r

library(Seurat)
library(emeansR)

obj <- NormalizeData(obj) |> FindVariableFeatures() |> ScaleData() |> RunPCA(npcs = 30)
pcs <- Embeddings(obj, "pca")[, 1:20]

fit <- emeans(pcs, k = 16, nepochs = 3, seed = 1)
obj$emeans <- factor(fit$cluster)
Idents(obj) <- "emeans"

obj <- RunUMAP(obj, dims = 1:20)
DimPlot(obj, group.by = "emeans")
```

## Citation

``` r

citation("emeansR")
```

Bessa S, Mazaré P-E, Szilvasy G, Touvron H, Picard D, Douze M, Jégou H
(2026). e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs).
arXiv:2611.09501.

# Package index

## Clustering

- [`emeans()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans.md) :
  e-means clustering
- [`predict(`*`<emeans>`*`)`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/predict.emeans.md)
  : Assign new data to e-means centers
- [`emeans_recipe()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans_recipe.md)
  : Inspect the e-means training recipe

## Streaming

- [`emeans_stream()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans_stream.md)
  [`emeans_stream_status()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans_stream.md)
  [`emeans_accumulate()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans_stream.md)
  [`emeans_update()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans_stream.md)
  [`emeans_end_epoch()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans_stream.md)
  [`emeans_finalize()`](https://toledoem.github.io/emeansR/reference/emeans_stream.md)
  : Streaming e-means for data that does not fit in memory
